newsitem.title: FRANCE: PLO diplomat says miracle needed for peace.
newsitem.headline: PLO diplomat says miracle needed for peace.

text.p: A senior Palestinian diplomat said on Friday it would take a miracle and the intervention of major powers to prevent the threat of war returning to the whole Middle East following bloody Israeli-Palestinian clashes.
PLO representative in France Leila Shahid told RMC radio that only full implementation of the Israeli-Palestinian peace accords could stop the violence.
"It needs a miracle and perhaps the intervention of the sponsors of the peace process, the United States, France, Europe to bring (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu to reason," she said.
"Barring this, we are heading into a new war situation not only in Palestinian territories, but in the whole Middle East," she said.
French newspapers squarely blamed Netanyahu for two days of gun battles in which more than 50 people died.

The left-wing daily Liberation also called on Western powers to step in, and added: "This would suppose the courage of pointing the finger at who is guilty -- Netanyahu's provocation -- and use coercion."

"(U.S. President Bill) Clinton's sluggish call for bilateral appeasement does not really go in that direction. And without the Americans, the other Western powers' voice can hardly be heard," it said.

The conservative Le Figaro said: "It is high time for the candidate, whose words pass, to turn into a prime minister whose acts remain. Otherwise Benjamin Netanyahu will be seen as a dangerous amateur."
"Israel's demand for absolute security will remain unrealistic if the cost is total insecurity for Palestinians," it said.
Israel and the Palestinian Authority, blaming each other for the violence, were seeking a summit to try to salvage five years of U.S.-driven peacemaking.
